biography: Nagendra Pavana is a Sanskrit scholar working on Vyākaraṇa, Sanskrit literature and Indian knowledge systems. He trained in the traditional gurukula system, including Vedāṅgas and the Mahābhāṣya, before earning a Ph.D. in Vyākaraṇa from Karnataka Samskrit University, Bengaluru. He has taught major Vyākaraṇa works for more than sixteen years and has contributed to Sanskrit e-learning resources with Vyoma Linguistic Labs. His interests include Pāṇinian grammar, Sanskrit poetry and aesthetics, Indian philosophy, the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, and Indian classical music.
researchOverview: His scholarly interests include Pāṇinian grammar and the Mahābhāṣya, Sanskrit poetry and aesthetics, Indian philosophical traditions, the Vedas and Vedāṅgas. His educational work also includes Sanskrit e-learning resources.

reviewNotes: The public teacher profile page displays placeholder text; the matching tutor_id 18984714 record in the publisher's teacher API supplies the biography and education details used here.
The API biography is undated; its statements about a six-year CVV appointment and an IIT Bombay project are retained as source-reported history, not as a complete 2026 employment timeline.
The Ph.D. thesis title is reproduced in Devanagari from the source. Degree years are unavailable.
Traditional gurukula training is included as non-degree education entries; it is not described as a university qualification.
Public CVV LMS listings establish past teaching, not a current semester assignment. Current teaching remains empty.
Students, patents, current office address, phone and a verified IIT Bombay email were not found and remain empty.
The IIM Bangalore record and PHI Learning record differ in author order; the publisher's PHI order is used.
A DK Printworld listing for a Bṛhatsaṃhitā volume was found, but its authorship and year were not independently confirmed, so it is not included.
The 2025 conference designations Project Research Scientist/Project Scientist III conflict with the site's Professor identity; identity fields are preserved.
